Coming back after a layoff

A six-week return plan for a runner who stopped for a month or more.

The first two weeks

Section 1

Runners come back too fast after a layoff. They know it while they are doing it, and they do it anyway.

The first two weeks feel easy and the third week hurts. That is the pattern most of them describe.

A plan that starts at half the old mileage looks timid on paper and works in practice.

Easy days should feel easy enough to hold a conversation the whole way round.

Strides come back in week two: short, relaxed, never a sprint.

The long run grows by one mile a week and drops back every fourth week.

Pain that changes the way you run is the signal to stop, not to push through.

Sleep counts as training. A short night undoes a good session.

Hills arrive in week four, once the legs remember what steady running feels like.

Most setbacks come from adding speed and distance in the same week.

A training log is the cheapest coach there is, and the most honest.

Race plans wait until six good weeks are behind you.
